import pandas as pd


def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    dim = inputs["dim_customer"].copy()
    stg = inputs["stg_customer"].copy()
    fact = inputs["fact_txn"].copy()

    dim = dim.reset_index(drop=True)

    # ---- Determine, for each customer_id, whether it has a current row and its segment ----
    current = dim[dim["is_current"] == 1]
    # In case of duplicate current rows (shouldn't normally happen), keep first encountered.
    current_map = current.drop_duplicates(subset=["customer_id"], keep="first") \
                          .set_index("customer_id")["segment"]

    def seg_differs(seg_s, seg_cur):
        s_na = pd.isna(seg_s)
        c_na = pd.isna(seg_cur)
        if s_na and c_na:
            return False
        if s_na != c_na:
            return True
        return seg_s != seg_cur

    creates_flags = []
    for _, row in stg.iterrows():
        cid = row["customer_id"]
        if cid not in current_map.index:
            creates_flags.append(True)
        else:
            cur_seg = current_map.loc[cid]
            creates_flags.append(seg_differs(row["segment"], cur_seg))

    stg = stg.copy()
    stg["_creates"] = creates_flags

    creating = stg[stg["_creates"]].copy()
    creating = creating.sort_values("customer_id", kind="mergesort").reset_index(drop=True)
    creating["_rn"] = range(1, len(creating) + 1)

    if len(dim) > 0:
        max_sk = dim["customer_sk"].max()
        if pd.isna(max_sk):
            max_sk = 0
    else:
        max_sk = 0

    creating["customer_sk"] = max_sk + creating["_rn"]

    # ---- Expire current rows for customers that get a new version ----
    cids_creating = set(creating["customer_id"].tolist())

    expire_mask = (dim["is_current"] == 1) & (dim["customer_id"].isin(cids_creating))

    update_date_map = creating.set_index("customer_id")["update_date"]

    if expire_mask.any():
        mapped_dates = dim.loc[expire_mask, "customer_id"].map(update_date_map)
        dim.loc[expire_mask, "eff_end_date"] = mapped_dates
        dim.loc[expire_mask, "is_current"] = 0

    # ---- Build new version rows ----
    new_rows = pd.DataFrame({
        "customer_sk": creating["customer_sk"],
        "customer_id": creating["customer_id"],
        "segment": creating["segment"],
        "eff_start_date": creating["update_date"],
        "eff_end_date": pd.NaT,
        "is_current": 1
    })

    dim_out = pd.concat([dim, new_rows], ignore_index=True, sort=False)

    # Ensure column order and types
    dim_out = dim_out[["customer_sk", "customer_id", "segment",
                        "eff_start_date", "eff_end_date", "is_current"]]
    dim_out["customer_sk"] = dim_out["customer_sk"].astype("int64")
    dim_out["customer_id"] = dim_out["customer_id"].astype("int64")
    dim_out["is_current"] = dim_out["is_current"].astype("int64")
    dim_out["eff_start_date"] = pd.to_datetime(dim_out["eff_start_date"])
    dim_out["eff_end_date"] = pd.to_datetime(dim_out["eff_end_date"])

    # ---- Step 2: key facts against the updated dimension ----
    def find_sk(row):
        cid = row["customer_id"]
        tdate = row["txn_date"]
        candidates = dim_out[dim_out["customer_id"] == cid]
        if candidates.empty:
            return -1
        start_ok = candidates["eff_start_date"] <= tdate
        end_ok = candidates["eff_end_date"].isna() | (tdate < candidates["eff_end_date"])
        matched = candidates[start_ok & end_ok]
        if matched.empty:
            return -1
        if len(matched) > 1:
            matched = matched.sort_values("eff_start_date", ascending=False)
        return int(matched.iloc[0]["customer_sk"])

    fact["customer_sk"] = fact.apply(find_sk, axis=1)
    fact_out = fact[["txn_id", "customer_sk", "amount"]].copy()
    fact_out["customer_sk"] = fact_out["customer_sk"].astype("int64")
    fact_out["txn_id"] = fact_out["txn_id"].astype("int64")
    fact_out["amount"] = fact_out["amount"].astype("float64")

    return {
        "dim_customer_out": dim_out.reset_index(drop=True),
        "fact_txn_keyed": fact_out.reset_index(drop=True)
    }
